title: Scorpion sting (Indian red scorpion) envenoming
subject: toxicology
setting: Primary health centre, emergency department, PICU/ICU
summary: Indian red scorpion stings cause an autonomic storm with myocardial dysfunction and pulmonary oedema, most dangerous in children. Give oral prazosin (30 mcg/kg in children, 500 mcg in adults, repeated 3-hourly by response) and scorpion antivenom 3 vials IV for grade 2 or higher; treat pulmonary oedema with dobutamine and vasodilators.

sections.title: Recognise and grade
items: Severe local pain and paraesthesia at the sting site. Systemic effects evolve within 30 minutes to 6 hours and usually settle within 1 to 2 days.

Early cholinergic phase (0 to 4 hours): vomiting, profuse sweating, salivation, priapism, bradycardia, hypotension. Later adrenergic phase (from about 4 hours, up to 48 hours): tachycardia, hypertension, cold extremities, pulmonary oedema.

Grade 1: local pain only. Grade 2: autonomic features (hypertension, sweating, vomiting, priapism, fever, shivering). Grades 3 and 4: pulmonary oedema, cardiogenic shock, hypotension, altered consciousness or multiorgan failure.
Children have the highest risk; most deaths are from myocardial dysfunction with pulmonary oedema. Other complications: seizures, encephalopathy, stroke, DIC, pancreatitis.

sections.title: Investigations
items: ECG (tachycardia, ST-T changes, ischaemic patterns), chest X-ray and echocardiography to detect myocardial dysfunction and pulmonary oedema.
Blood glucose (often raised), potassium, renal and liver function, amylase and LDH; troponin where available.
Vital signs every 30 minutes for 3 hours, hourly for the next 6 hours, then every 4 hours until improvement (IAP).

sections.title: Initial care
items: Pain: paracetamol 15 mg/kg (adult 1 g) orally or IV every 4 to 6 hours; ice packs and local infiltration of lignocaine without adrenaline for severe pain.
IV access; oral fluids if tolerated. If IV fluids are needed use 0.9% saline or Ringer lactate cautiously, balancing hypovolaemia from vomiting and sweating against pulmonary oedema risk.
Agitation: midazolam or diazepam 0.05 to 0.1 mg/kg IV.
Admit anyone with systemic features; PICU or ICU for grade 3 or 4.

sections.title: Prazosin and scorpion antivenom
items: Prazosin for every patient with an autonomic storm (grade 2 or higher): children 30 mcg/kg per dose orally; adults 500 mcg (0.5 mg) orally. Give by nasogastric tube if vomiting. Do not give as prophylaxis when pain is the only symptom.

Repeat prazosin every 3 hours according to response until extremities are warm and dry and peripheral veins are easily visible; most patients need 4 doses or fewer. Use ordinary 1 mg tablets, not sustained-release forms.
First-dose hypotension: keep the patient lying down after each dose; parents should not lift the child up.
Scorpion antivenom (Haffkine monovalent SAV): 30 mL (3 vials) diluted in 100 mL 0.9% saline IV over 30 minutes for grade 2 or higher, irrespective of age and weight. Give as early as possible.
SAV plus prazosin gave faster recovery, less progression to grade 3 or 4 and lower prazosin needs than prazosin alone in an Indian paediatric RCT.
SAV reaction: stop the infusion and give supportive treatment; once stable, restart at a constant rate over 1 hour.

sections.title: Pulmonary oedema and shock
items: Oxygen, sit up, and non-invasive or mechanical ventilation as needed.
Myocardial dysfunction or hypotension: dobutamine 5 to 15 mcg/kg/min.

Vasodilator for pulmonary oedema: sodium nitroprusside 0.3 to 5 mcg/kg/min, or nitroglycerine (children 0.1 to 1 mcg/kg/min; adults start 10 mcg/min, doubling every 5 minutes, keeping systolic BP above 90 mmHg). Give prazosin 1 hour before stopping nitroprusside.
Diuretics only if there is fluid overload with impaired renal water excretion. Avoid morphine, which can worsen arrhythmias.
Atropine only for severe bradycardia with hypotension: 0.5 mg IV (children 0.02 mg/kg); it can intensify the adrenergic phase.

sections.title: Prevention
items: Shake out shoes, clothes and bedding before use.
Clear debris, trash and stacked material around the house; clean school rooms and furniture before reopening after holidays.
Sleep on cots with mosquito nets, and do not put hands into places you cannot see.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Discharging a child with sweating and vomiting: grade 2 can progress to pulmonary oedema within hours.
Routine atropine for sweating and salivation.
Treating hypertension with nifedipine, captopril or other vasodilators instead of prazosin (reflex tachycardia, adverse effects).
Sustained-release prazosin, or prophylactic prazosin for pain alone.
Liberal IV fluids during the adrenergic phase.

drugs.name: Prazosin
drugs.dose: Children 30 mcg/kg orally; adults 500 mcg (0.5 mg) orally; repeat every 3 hours according to response
drugs.notes: Plain 1 mg tablets; keep supine after doses; usually 4 doses or fewer.

drugs.name: Scorpion antivenom (Haffkine monovalent)
drugs.dose: 30 mL (3 vials) in 100 mL 0.9% saline IV over 30 minutes, single dose
drugs.notes: Grade 2 and above, any age or weight.

drugs.name: Sodium nitroprusside
drugs.notes: Pulmonary oedema; start prazosin 1 hour before stopping.

drugs.name: Nitroglycerine
drugs.dose: Adults 10 mcg/min IV, double every 5 minutes to effect; children 0.1 to 1 mcg/kg/min
drugs.notes: Keep systolic BP above 90 mmHg in adults.

drugs.name: Paracetamol
drugs.dose: 15 mg/kg orally or IV every 4 to 6 hours (adult 1 g; max 4 g/day)
